name: Rotate MD-11
description: Rotate MD-11F and MD-11P on X-Plane. The flap handle is the aircraft's own, so the flap position is read from Rotate/aircraft/controls/flap_handle rather than from the stock flap handle dataref, which this aircraft leaves at zero.
notes: The stock handle dataref reads zero for the whole flight on this aircraft, and the server normalises flaps against the largest value it saw in the flight, so a flight that never reports flaps has no flap position at all: every approach fails the stabilised-approach check with the flaps "at unknown". HubHop has no readable Rotate MD-11 entries; the handle variable is the one the SmartCopilot shared-cockpit configuration for this aircraft synchronises (github.com/radonthetyrant/smartcopilot-rotate-md-11), next to flap_to_sel (the DIAL-A-FLAP thumbwheel) and flap_lim_sel. Its scale is taken to be a 0-1 ratio of handle travel, which is how Rotate's MD-80 publishes its handle (Rotate/md80/systems/flap_handle_drag_position_ratio); that has not been confirmed in the simulator, and if it proves to be degrees or a detent index only the scale step needs changing. On X-Plane every source is a dataref, so a candidate list would always use the first one, and a dataref X-Plane cannot resolve does not fail: it reports nothing, or zero. The handle and the stock dataref are therefore combined with max: whichever one the aircraft actually drives wins, and an MD-11 that is not Rotate's keeps the stock reading. Both are rounded to a whole percent because the server truncates the value and treats any drop between two samples as the flaps retracting.
